regulatory_and_risk_profile: Explainability required for claim and pricing denials
Legacy policy-administration systems with limited APIs
paper_process_blockers: Actuarial review of any pricing model change
Regulatory filing clocks for rate or form changes
Compliance review of claims-handling changes before automation touches live files
Change requests to the core policy system
dominant_friction: Combined-ratio pressure makes every change look expensive, and every denial must be explainable to a regulator.
value_frame: Anchor on loss-ratio compression, claims cycle-time reduction, human-in-the-loop audit trails, and elastic peak-volume pricing.

buying_committee.primary_fear: Automated pricing drifts, and we find out only after a bad loss year.
Automation denies a valid claim and triggers a regulatory complaint.
We cannot explain a denial to a regulator in plain language.
A model change goes live without actuarial sign-off.

signature_objections: Our combined ratio is already under pressure. Why would we add a new variable cost line?
When a claim gets denied by your model, what does the adjuster tell the policyholder?
Catastrophe season triples our claim volume for six weeks. Does your pricing spike with it?

metrics.speaker: Chief Underwriting Officer
metrics.setup: Claims cycle time is the number everyone here watches.
metrics.partial: We track cycle time and loss ratio every month, and the board counts every point, but the AI piece is not in the scorecard yet.
metrics.verbatim: Cycle time from twenty-one days to seven, and at least two points on loss ratio, or this does not get funded.

economic_buyer.speaker: Head of Claims
economic_buyer.setup: Claims would be the first team to use tools like this, so I can sponsor the pilot.
economic_buyer.partial: I can approve claims tools up to a pilot cap. Shared tools get more complicated.
economic_buyer.verbatim: The pilot comes out of my claims operations budget, and I approve it alone. The production tier goes to the CFO.

decision_criteria.speaker: General Counsel
decision_criteria.setup: Compliance will score every vendor, and explainability and fair-claims rules are at the top of the list.
decision_criteria.partial: Both carry the most weight for my team. Explainability would probably break a tie.
decision_criteria.verbatim: A denial without a plain-language reason an adjuster can read to a policyholder. We will not go live without that.

decision_process.speaker: General Counsel
decision_process.setup: After a pilot, nothing moves here without the right reviews.
decision_process.partial: It depends what the pilot touches. Pricing goes through actuarial review, and anything on live claim files goes through compliance.
decision_process.verbatim: Compliance approves the claims-handling change before any live claim file is touched. If pricing is affected, actuarial review and a rate filing follow on a sixty-day clock.

paper_process.speaker: General Counsel
paper_process.setup: Legal and compliance will want to see exactly how this changes our claims handling.
paper_process.partial: They can look early, but no automation runs on live claim files until compliance signs off.
paper_process.verbatim: About six weeks from the day they receive the claims-handling change.

identify_pain.speaker: Head of Claims
identify_pain.setup: Simple claims are piling up, and we think severity leakage on them is getting worse.
identify_pain.partial: Real money, though we have not pinned it down. Adjusters are buried in simple claims, and the backlog keeps growing with catastrophe season coming.
identify_pain.verbatim: We already have 4,000 open claims. Another catastrophe season on top of that, and severity leakage on simple auto claims gets worse every quarter.

champion.speaker: Chief Underwriting Officer
champion.setup: Leadership will want to hear about this from one of us, and the regulators will ask questions after.
champion.partial: I would back it. My team has been asking for something like this. The regulators are what worries me.
champion.verbatim: The audit trail design in writing. With that, I will take this to the leadership team myself.

competition.speaker: Head of Claims
competition.setup: Our core policy vendor has been pitching us too.
competition.partial: Doing nothing is not really an option. Their claims module is one we have been meaning to look at.
competition.verbatim: They are offering their claims automation free if we renew, so you have to show a better loss-ratio case than that.

veto_holder.reason: Every automated claim decision needs a reason an adjuster can read to a policyholder.

metrics.open: What number has to move on claims cycle time for this to be worth it, and by when?
metrics.pin: How much do you need to cut cycle time, and how many points of loss ratio must it improve?

economic_buyer.open: Who signs the PO for claims tools, and up to what amount?
economic_buyer.pin: Beyond the pilot cap, whose budget does this come out of, and who has the final sign-off?

decision_criteria.open: How will you score vendors on explainability and fair-claims compliance? Which criterion breaks a tie?
decision_criteria.pin: What would rule us out with your compliance team, regardless of price?

decision_process.open: After a successful pilot, what happens on day one, day ten and day thirty?
decision_process.pin: Who else needs to approve before a live claim file is touched? Walk me through the approval path.

paper_process.open: Can legal and compliance start reviewing the claims-handling change in parallel with the pilot?
paper_process.pin: How long does the compliance review take before automation can run on a live claim file?

identify_pain.open: What does severity leakage on simple claims cost you each quarter?
identify_pain.pin: What happens if you do nothing and the backlog keeps growing through catastrophe season?

champion.open: If I am not in the room, how would you make the case to the leadership team?
champion.pin: What would you need to take this to leadership and the regulators with confidence?

competition.open: What happens if you build this in-house with your core vendor, or do nothing?
competition.pin: What are you comparing us against, including your core policy vendor's claims module?

account_research.buyer_line: What do you already know about how we run claims here?
account_research.strong: I saw your simple auto claims now route through a new triage desk. What prompted that?

discovery_questioning.strong: Walk me through how a simple claim gets handled today, start to finish.

listening_summarizing.buyer_line: One thing before we go on. The bigger issue for us is the backlog on simple claims, not the complex ones.
listening_summarizing.strong: So the real cost is the simple-claim backlog, not the complex claims. Did I get that right?

commercial_insight.strong: Carriers like yours lose more to severity leakage on simple claims than to fraud. Here is the number.

value_messaging.strong: Today, twenty-one days per simple claim. After, seven, proven with a carrier your size.

answer_first.strong: My recommendation: start with simple auto claims. Three reasons.

identify_pain.strong: What does a slow claim cost you each month, in adjuster hours and leakage?

champion.strong: If I am not in the room, how would you make the case to your Chief Underwriting Officer?

paper_process.speaker: General Counsel
paper_process.setup: The pilot ran on closed claim files. Moving onto open claims means legal and compliance review it again.
paper_process.partial: They can start early. Open claims also trigger state notice rules in two of our states.
paper_process.verbatim: Seven weeks for the open-claims review, and the two state notices go out first. Start now and you are live before storm season.

decision_process.speaker: General Counsel
decision_process.setup: Simple auto claims are live. Claims now wants the same on property, and that is a new approval.
decision_process.partial: Property changes the claims-handling guidelines, so compliance and the actuaries both review it. The order is not set.
decision_process.verbatim: Actuarial signs off the reserving impact first, then compliance approves the new guidelines, then the Head of Claims launches. About eight weeks.

economic_buyer.speaker: Head of Claims
economic_buyer.setup: Adding property takes this past my pilot budget, so the funding changes.
economic_buyer.partial: Auto came out of my operations budget. Property sits under a different line of business, so some costs would be shared.
economic_buyer.verbatim: The property line pays for its own usage, and the CFO signs anything shared across lines. I keep approving auto.

competition.speaker: Head of Claims
competition.setup: Our cloud provider now offers a claims document service natively, and it is cheaper on paper.
competition.partial: It is cheaper per page. Our data team also thinks they could rebuild your workflow on it.
competition.verbatim: We would compare you to the native service and a rebuild by our data team. You win only if your loss-ratio case beats both.

metrics.speaker: Chief Underwriting Officer
metrics.setup: I will back a bigger commit only on numbers from live claims, not the pilot.
metrics.partial: Auto cycle time came down. For property, the board watches reopened claims as closely as speed.
metrics.verbatim: Property cycle time down by a third within two quarters, with reopened claims under four percent.

identify_pain.speaker: Head of Claims
identify_pain.setup: Adjusters stopped using the tool on anything beyond the simplest auto claims.
identify_pain.partial: They trust it for glass and towing, but still key in the rest by hand. So the backlog barely moved.
identify_pain.verbatim: We pay for automation and still staff the full adjuster bench for anything above glass. That is two cost bases on one backlog.

paper_process.open: Can legal and compliance start reviewing open claims now, in parallel with the pilot?
paper_process.pin: How long does the compliance review take once the state notice rules are in scope?

decision_process.open: For property, what are the steps from live auto claims to production?
decision_process.pin: Who else needs to approve after compliance and the actuaries? Walk me through the approval path.

economic_buyer.open: With property in scope, whose budget does this come out of?
economic_buyer.pin: Who signs for the property line, and who has the final sign-off on shared costs?

competition.open: Would you use the cheaper native service, or do nothing?
competition.pin: What are you comparing us against: the native service, or a rebuild by your data team?

metrics.open: Which number must hold on live claims before you back anything bigger?
metrics.pin: How much do you need to cut property cycle time, and where must reopened claims sit?

identify_pain.open: What does it cost you when adjusters stop using the tool?
identify_pain.pin: What happens if you do nothing and adjusters still key the rest in by hand?
